solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nameless criminals, funny guys

indicators.note: less of a name: N, the abbreviation for name, is taken out of the criminals

parts.note: gangsters are organised criminals

explanation.surface: A gang of anonymous crooks who are also, oddly, a bunch of comedians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nameless' reads as anonymous but means drop N (name) from GANGSTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A gagster is a comedian who tells jokes, so the plural is a set of funny men.

clue.text: Maybe a tea bag will have become ruined

definitions.text: Maybe a tea bag will have become ruined

parts.words: Maybe a tea bag will have become ruined
parts.note: a used tea bag has literally been put into the teapot, and the same phrase is an idiom for falling into ruin

explanation.surface: A sad tea bag that has been spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: The literal reading (the bag has been placed in the teapot) sits on the idiom meaning deteriorated.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for something that has deteriorated badly, said of a business or garden, means it has become ruined.

clue.text: Sort of drug information given to man

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Eric is a man's name

explanation.surface: A pharmacist hands a man the leaflet about a type of medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A generic drug is one sold under its chemical name rather than a brand, so it is a kind of medicine.

clue.text: Old drum makes little boy dance endlessly

parts.note: Tim, short for Timothy, is a boy's name

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the dance word is cut off

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: An antique drum gets a young lad dancing on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' looks like 'without stopping' but trims the last L from BALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A timbal is an archaic kettledrum, so it is an old percussion instrument.

clue.text: Get torn apart about imperial measure being given up

indicators.note: the tearing word sits about, that is around, the measure

parts.note: rend means tear apart, the command to get something torn
an ounce is a unit in the imperial system of weights

explanation.surface: Someone rips up the old imperial measures as they are abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Renounced means formally abandoned, so it matches something being given up; past participle in both.

clue.text: Compliant priest, having returned to GP?

parts.note: a GP (general practitioner) is a family doctor, a doc

indicators.note: returned means read backwards, so the priest's name is turned round

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: An obliging clergyman goes back to see his doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned to' suggests the priest paying a visit; in fact 'having returned' turns the priest's name round, and 'to' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Docile means easily managed and obedient, a synonym of compliant.

clue.text: Is Henry appearing in transvestite attire? Just a bit of cloth

indicators.note: the first pieces appear inside the outfit word, so they are put within it

parts.note: drag is clothing of the opposite sex worn by a performer
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Henry has turned up in women's clothing, only to find a scrap of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: H (henry) is the SI unit, a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishrag is a dishcloth, an ordinary scrap of fabric for washing up.

clue.text: Box with bitd of food — they may seem stale

parts.note: a chest is a large box
nuts are small bits of food; 'bitd' is a typing slip for 'bits'

explanation.surface: A crate of snacks that might have gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: Chestnuts here are old, overused jokes, not the nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: An old chestnut is a joke or story told so often it has grown tired and stale.

clue.text: Shrub worker found in wood

indicators.note: the worker is found inside the wood, so it is placed within it

parts.note: lana is the hard wood of the genipap tree
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A labourer discovered among the trees beside a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: LANA is an obscure timber name, a dictionary sense rather than a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Lantana is a tropical flowering bush of the verbena family, grown in gardens.

clue.text: Religious father of Joshua

definitions.meaning: used as a noun, a religious is a member of an order, such as a sister in a convent
in the Bible Joshua is called the son of ...

explanation.surface: A devout man who fathered the biblical Joshua.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Religious' is a noun here: a member of a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman in a convent is a religious, and the biblical patriarch shares that same three-letter name.

clue.text: Some gannet munched fruit

indicators.note: munched suggests chewed up, so these letters are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A seabird gobbles up some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The mangosteen is a tropical tree's sweet, purple-skinned edible produce.

clue.text: Someone ferocious to you and me, creating hell

parts.note: a tartar is a fierce, violent person
us is the pronoun for you and me together

explanation.surface: A savage person who makes life a torment for the pair of us.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartarus is the abyss of the underworld in Greek myth, a classical name for the infernal regions.

clue.text: Cane to beat rotten fellow earlier

indicators.note: the fellow comes earlier, placed in front of the beating word

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible, treacherous man
to tan is to beat, as in tanning someone's hide

explanation.surface: A cane is used to thrash a scoundrel before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cane' looks like a verb next to 'beat', but it is the noun defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattan is the climbing palm whose stems make canes and wickerwork.

clue.text: Agreement will make president do something

parts.note: to act is to do something

explanation.surface: A deal that forces the head of state to take action.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal treaty or accord between parties.

clue.text: Cry of pain with daughter in built-up area coming to ground

indicators.note: the cry and the daughter go in, inside the urban word

parts.note: a town is a built-up area
ouch is what one cries when hurt

explanation.surface: A girl yelps in a town as something lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Touchdown is an aircraft's landing, the moment it meets the earth; both are nouns of action.

clue.text: Initially cook is arguing about cake ingredient

indicators.note: about can mean in a mixed state, so these letters are scattered and reformed
initially takes just the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A baker starts by quarrelling over what goes in the sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: C (the start of cook) joins IS ARGUING in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing sugar is the fine powdered sweetener used for frosting and decorating bakes.

clue.text: His rude son, shunning Society, badly brought up

indicators.note: badly shows the letters are put together wrongly, so they are rearranged
shunning means avoiding, so the society letter is left out

explanation.surface: An ill-mannered lad shunned by polite company, raised poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly brought up' reads as one phrase, but 'badly' is the anagram signal on HIRUDEON-style letters left after dropping one S.
explanation.definitionFit: Nourished means fed and reared, so a child nourished has been raised.

clue.text: Groups of soldiers organised meetings after end of war

indicators.note: the shuffled letters come after the single letter
the end of a word is its final letter
organised means arranged, so these letters are put into order afresh

explanation.surface: Assemblies arranged once the fighting stops.
explanation.definitionFit: Regiments are permanent army units, each a body of troops.

clue.text: Our tour goes awry with the introduction of terrible singer

indicators.note: introduction means bringing something in, so the bad word is put inside
going awry means going wrong, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: bad is a synonym of terrible

explanation.surface: A concert trip falls apart once an awful vocalist joins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes awry' shuffles the first two words, and 'with the introduction of' slips the synonym for terrible into the middle of that shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A troubadour was a medieval lyric poet who sang his verses, a wandering minstrel.

clue.text: A clue to OUP's gathering in of information, say?

parts.note: O, a round letter, followed by UP spells the clue's OUP, so the answer read as instructions builds it

explanation.surface: A hint about what Oxford University Press collects.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as wordplay (a ring shape, then UP) yields OUP. OUP is Oxford University Press.
explanation.definitionFit: A summary or collection of the news is called a round-up, pulling facts together.

clue.text: Land area needing care having got churned up over time

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits over, above, the second
churned up means stirred about, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Fields that need looking after have been ploughed up over the years.
explanation.definitionFit: Acreage is an extent of land measured in acres.

clue.text: Bird protected by English agriculturalists

indicators.note: the bird is sheltered within the letters of these words, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A rare bird is safeguarded by farmers in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The shag is a seabird, a cousin of the cormorant.

clue.text: A "distressing" operation

parts.note: read as de-tressing, removing tresses or locks of hair, not causing upset

explanation.surface: A surgical procedure that upsets the patient.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks flag a second reading: dis-tressing, taking away tresses.
explanation.definitionFit: A trim at the barber's removes tresses, so it literally un-tresses the head.

clue.text: Sponsor a couple of boys?

parts.note: Pat is one boy's name
Ron is a second boy's name

explanation.surface: A backer who is just a pair of lads.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron is a benefactor who supports an artist or cause with money.

clue.text: One reformer or another ignoring King

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so the King part is dropped

parts.note: the other reformer is Martin Luther King, the civil rights leader
King is taken as written

explanation.surface: Naming one religious reformer or a second, but without the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Martin Luther King minus King leaves the name of the earlier Martin, the German Protestant reformer.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Luther began the Protestant Reformation in 1517, the archetypal church reformer.

clue.text: Test drink — one put in animals' enclosure

parts.note: a viva is an oral examination at university

indicators.note: the numeral is put in, placed inside the spirit

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An exam on drinking, with somebody kept in a zoo pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A vivarium is a tank or cage where live creatures are kept in near-natural conditions.

clue.text: Go to bed at the seaside?

definitions.text: Go to bed at the seaside?

parts.words: Go to bed at the seaside?
parts.note: a ship's anchor goes down to the seabed, not someone retiring for the night

explanation.surface: Turning in for the night on holiday at the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is the seabed: the anchor sinks to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowering a ship's mooring weight sends it down to the seabed.

clue.text: Prisoner to trick politician briefly

definitions.meaning: a convict, an inmate in jail
short for Conservative, a Tory politician

explanation.surface: A jailbird out to fool a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: a convict, to swindle, and the short form of Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: The short word covers a convict, a swindle and an abbreviated Conservative, three senses in one.

clue.text: Drunk creating a stink in the Home Counties

indicators.note: the smell goes in, inside the region's letters

parts.note: the Home Counties are the counties around London, in the South East (SE) of England
pong is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A boozer making a smell in the commuter belt round London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' is a noun, a heavy drinker, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge is slang for a heavy drinker who soaks up alcohol.

clue.text: Port — it is creating a type of inflammation

parts.note: Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A drinker claims port causes swelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the wine but is the Yemeni harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Adenitis is swelling of a gland, especially a lymph gland, a medical condition.
